subject: Capacity handshake: OEM queueing + cloud backstop for ACME deal
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Beth Hudson <beth.hudson@acmeai.com>, sales@nexaoem.com, cloud-sales@aethercloud.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 25 Oct 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity handshake: OEM queueing + cloud backstop for ACME deal

Hi Beth / Nexa / Aether team —

Thanks again for the productive call last week. As ACME moves toward contract signature (ACME-2026-110) we want to lock an executable plan for dedicated capacity on a timeline that matches the Q1 onboarding window Beth outlined. Two immediate constraints surfaced: (1) OEM manufacturing queue for the specific P40-G2 SKU is lengthening (Nexa, see ETA below) and (2) cloud reserved capacity backstops are available only in limited tranche windows.

Goal: agree on a "handshake" that stitches OEM partial shipments + cloud reservation fallback so ACME gets predictable capacity for first 8 weeks of production while full fleet arrives. Proposed approach follows — open to suggestions.

Proposed stitch plan (high level):
- Staged deliveries: Nexa provides early tranche (~25% of committed cards) on a prioritized lane for Redwood/ACME, with milestones and partial invoicing.
- Cloud backstop: Aether to reserve on-demand reserved pools for the ramp weeks (weeks 1-8) that can be released if OEM tranche is on-time; pricing should reflect conversion credit if tranche fulfills.
- SKU lane balancing: hold a small buffer of mixed-quant SKUs (8-bit/4-bit) so we can run critical production on highest-perf subset while full inventory completes.
- Contract mechanics: DocuSign quote + PO cadence, acceptance of partial shipments, and SLA for lead-time variance (X days).

Immediate asks:
1) Nexa — confirm per-tranche ETA for P40-G2 and your willingness to split shipment and invoice (attach quote).
2) Aether — confirm reservation window XLS (capacity units by week) and a conversion credit model if reservations are used fewer weeks.
3) Ben/Karthik/Laura — internal confirmation on acceptance criteria for partial capacity (what % of model coverage we consider "sufficient" to avoid escalation).

I attached the Nexa quote and Aether reservation template for reference.

Thanks —
Rishi

Rishi Malhotra

Hi Rishi / Beth / team —

Thanks for the clear plan. Quick answers below; see attached marked-up quote (nexa_quote_Q4-2026.pdf).

ETA and tranche proposal:
- Current manufacturing queue projects earliest full-rack shipments in late Jan 2027 (calendar-week 4 of Q1).
- We can prioritize a "fast-lane" 25% tranche to ship by Dec 20, 2026 if PO and 30% deposit are confirmed by Nov 5.
- Second tranche (remaining 75%) follows normal queue with target ship-by Jan 28, 2027.

Partial shipments & invoicing:
- We will accept split invoicing with milestone payment tied to shipment date. We can include a provision that converts deposit to credit against the first tranche in the event of cancellation.

Lead-time risk & escalation:
- If upstream wafer shortages delay the fast lane we propose a 10-business-day padding and an automatic notification to Redwood procurement.
- We can also hold 2% hot-swap spares in a regional depot (cost + small recurring storage fee).

Action items from Nexa:
1) Confirm PO threshold for the fast-lane (we propose minimum 100 cards).
2) Confirm whether Redwood will accept 30% deposit for tranche 1 and 70% on full delivery.
3) Nominate Redwood contact for weekly cadence on manufacturing updates (we propose weekly Tue updates).

Let us know and we can publish a formal SOW amendment.

--

Marcus / Rishi / team —

Appreciate the agility on the fast-lane tranche. A few internal constraints / clarifications from the product & finance side: 

- Acceptance criteria: for we consider the initial tranche "sufficient" to avoid service-level escalation if it enables 75% of peak QPS for the first 6 weeks (roughly translates to X tokens/sec and benchmark run). Karthik, can you confirm that 25% of cards meets 75% of matched throughput for our common config?
- PO and deposit: finance will accept 30% deposit but need clear refund/conversion rules documented in the SOW (Nexa: please add conversion credit language).
- Cloud backstop billing: Aether, if we reserve for weeks 1-8 and only use weeks 1-4, we need a conversion credit applied to committed reserved price so ACME isn't double-billed. The credit can be applied to Redwood invoices for ACME.
- Contingency: If both OEM & cloud fail to meet week-1 capacity, we will run a controlled soft-launch and prioritize traffic (critical endpoints only).

Immediate internal asks: Karthik / Laura — please review the attached tech acceptance checklist and confirm by EOD Thursday so we can align purchase timing.

Thanks —
Ben

Thanks all — this is very helpful. A couple notes from ACME side: 

- We approve the fast-lane tranche plan provided the PO window and deposit schedule is kept tight. Nov 5 PO cutoff works for us; we can expedite on our side.
- We also want documented escalation SLAs if Nexa misses the Dec tranche by >15 business days — specifically a commitment to priority placement in the next available fabric (or a cash penalty).
- Cloud-backstop: ACME prefers an automatic conversion where unused reserved weeks convert to a credit that Redwood applies to our onboarding invoice. If Aether wants Redwood to invoice, happy as long as there's transparency of credits.

Next steps: 
1) Rishi / Ben — please circulate the updated SOW language and the PO template by EOD Friday.
2) Marcus — please add the conversion-credit clause and the 15-business-day penalty option into the quote and confirm minimum PO quantity.
3) Aether — please send a filled reservation window XLS with week-by-week capacity and the credit formula so ACME procurement can sign.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Beth
